drivingQuestion: Does R' Akiva concede that a female burnt offering that ascended the altar must descend?
outcomeNote: the baraita is re-read to concern sacrificial portions, so R' Zeira's objection falls and R' Chiyya bar Abba's statement stands

segments.he: תְּנַן הָתָם: וּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִין; רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַכְשִׁיר בְּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִים.
segments.en: § The baraita cited by Rabba is now discussed in a different context: «We learned» in a mishna «there» (84a) that if disqualified offerings are nevertheless brought upon the altar, they are removed, «and blemished» animals are also included in this halakha. «Rabbi Akiva deems blemished» animals «fit,» and if they were brought upon the altar they are not removed.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא הִכְשִׁיר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אֶלָּא בְּדוּקִּין שֶׁבָּעַיִן, הוֹאִיל וּכְשֵׁירִים בְּעוֹפוֹת. וְהוּא שֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁהּ אֶת מוּמָהּ.
segments.en: «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Rabbi Akiva deemed fit only» an animal with a blemish «on the cornea of the eye» and similar blemishes that are not noticeable, «since they are valid in» the case of «birds. And» in addition, this «is» the halakha provided «that its consecration preceded its blemish,» i.e., when the animal was consecrated it was still entirely fit.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּעוֹלַת נְקֵבָה, דִּכְמַאן דִּקְדַם מוּמָהּ לְהֶקְדֵּישָׁהּ דָּמֵי.
segments.en: «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says: And Rabbi Akiva concedes with regard to a female burnt offering» that was brought upon the altar «that» since a burnt offering may be only a male animal, «it is comparable to» a case «where its blemish preceded its consecration,» since the disqualifying factor was there from the outset. Therefore, if it was brought upon the altar it must be removed.

segments.he: מֵתִיב רַבִּי זֵירָא: הַמַּעֲלֶה מֵהֶן בַּחוּץ – פָּטוּר. הָא מֵאִימָּן – חַיָּיב; וְהֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ? בְּעוֹלַת נְקֵבָה.
segments.en: «Rabbi Zeira raises an objection» to this from the baraita cited by Rabba: «One who offers up» one «of these outside» the Temple is «exempt,» as they are not fit to be sacrificed on the altar. «But» it can be inferred that if he were to sacrifice «from» the flesh of the «mother of» one of «these» outside the Temple, he would be «liable. And how can you find these» circumstances? It is only «in» the case of «a female burnt offering.» This is because with regard to a peace offering, which may also be from a female animal, its flesh is not burned on the altar but is eaten. Therefore, there would be no liability for sacrificing it outside the Temple.

segments.he: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא קָסָבַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עוֹלַת נְקֵבָה אִם עָלְתָה לֹא תֵּרֵד, הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא. אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ אִם עָלְתָה תֵּרֵד, הָא מַנִּי?
segments.en: Rabbi Zeira explains his objection: «Granted, if you say» that «Rabbi Akiva holds» with regard to «a female burnt offering» that «if it ascended» onto the altar «it does not descend,» in accordance with «whose» opinion «is this» baraita? It «is» that of «Rabbi Akiva.» This is because one is liable for sacrificing any offering outside the Temple that may be sacrificed on the altar, including one that was brought upon the altar inappropriately but is not removed. «But if you say» that with regard to a female burnt offering «if it ascended» the altar «it» must «descend,» and it entirely lacks the status of an offering fit to be sacrificed on the altar, in accordance with «whose» opinion «is this» baraita?

segments.he: אֵימָא: הַמַּעֲלֶה מֵהֶן בַּחוּץ – פָּטוּר, הָא מֵאֵימוּרֵי אִימָּן – חַיָּיב.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Say» that the inference should be as follows: «One who offers up» one «of those» items «outside» the Temple is «exempt, but» if he sacrificed «from the sacrificial portions of» the «mother of» one of «these,» he is «liable.» This halakha can apply to both a sin offering and a peace offering, for which a female may be brought and whose sacrificial portions are burned on the altar.

segments.he: וְהָא ״מֵהֶן״ קָתָנֵי – וְאִימָּן דּוּמְיָא דִּידְהוּ! אֶלָּא אֵימָא: הַמַּעֲלֶה מֵאֵימוּרֵיהֶן בַּחוּץ – פָּטוּר, הָא מֵאֵימוּרֵי אִימָּן – חַיָּיב.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: «But» the baraita «teaches» this halakha with the term: «Of» one of «these,» indicating that it is referring to one who sacrifices the flesh, and not the sacrificial portions alone. «And» the case of «their mother» is «similar to» that of «them,» and is therefore referring to sacrificing the flesh of the mother outside the Temple, and not the sacrificial portions. «Rather, say» as follows: «One who offers up» part «of their sacrificial portions outside» the Temple is «exempt, but» one who offered up some «of the sacrificial portions of» the «mother of» one of «these» is «liable.»
